## RCA — confirmed at runtime on current `origin/main` (post-1957, post-1983)

### Ticket still stands after both landings

- **1957** (`irongrey-chubby-oxpecker`, aa7b) repaired the PRIMARY id-identity skip. It
  does not touch the comparison key, so the SECONDARY body-equality layer this ticket is
  about is unchanged — and it is precisely the layer that guards a lost map write.
- **1983** (`unreal-empathetic-illadopsis`, 5931) DID change what lands: `fit_preserving_marker`
  now reserves budget for `RECONCILER_MARKER`, so the landed body is
  `<content prefix><vendor notice>` re-decorated. The divergence this ticket describes
  survives and gained a SECOND component (the marker budget the differ key does not model).
  So the ticket is **not obsolete**; its mechanism is real and its numbers moved.

### Proven mechanism (driven, not read)

Driving the real Cloud objects (`_JiraSanitizer`, `AdfCodec`, `outbound_comments`) with a
43,200-char body on current main:

```
compare key len  = 32767   (sanitizer.fit_comment -> truncate_comment_body, PLAIN 32,767)
landed body len  = 31753   (fit_preserving_marker(decorate(b), AdfCodec.fit_outbound),
                            SERIALIZED-ADF 32,000, minus the marker budget)
EQUAL?           = False   (first divergence at index 31725)
```

In-limit bodies converge (short, multi-line 20k, unicode, empty all EQUAL); the divergence
is confined to the over-length regime, and it begins around **plain length ~31.8k** (where
the ADF serialization first crosses 32,000), not at 32,767.

### The good -> bad transition (discriminating experiment)

Re-ran the same two transforms at `27b868ba55^` (a detached worktree):

```
PRE-27b868ba55: cmp=32767  landed=32767  EQUAL=True
```

Before that commit both paths ran the SAME shared helper (`add_comment` called
`_sanitize_comment` -> `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body`). `27b868ba55` replaced the
send-path fit with `codec.fit_outbound` (the ADF/description fitter) and left
`_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` on `truncate_comment_body`. That is the divergence, and it
rules out "pre-existing since 6afc".

### Defect legitimacy: `defect`, cited

`comment_limits.py`'s module docstring states the invariant as a hard requirement: *"If the
two paths used different truncation logic they could never agree on the landed body, and the
loop would persist. They MUST therefore share this one helper so they cannot drift."*
`_diff_comments`'s own docstring asserts "the send path truncates an over-length body to
Jira's 32,767-char limit" — a statement that is now FALSE.

### Defect origin

`caused_by` = **789c-1251-fc21-4cf6** (`emersed-specific-mutt`), commit `27b868ba55`,
2026-08-13. Not the file the fix lands in and not a blame-majority answer: this is the change
that moved the send path off the shared fitter while the differ stayed on it. Its own review
demoted body-equality to SECONDARY in the same commit, so it is exactly the work item where
the divergence could have been caught. Close class: `regression`.

### A THIRD, separate divergence found (not this ticket)

This project runs `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"` (rebar.toml:87), i.e. rich mode is ON. Under
rich the local key is normalized with `AdfCodec.normalize_outbound` (markdown round trip,
which ESCAPES `[`/`]`) while the Jira side is decoded with `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`
(`adf_to_text`, no escaping). So a markdown comment WELL WITHIN the limit already fails
body-equality today:

```
rich=True, in-limit markdown:  local '[link](<http://x>)'  vs landed '[link](http://x)'   -> no match
```

That is a decode asymmetry, not a fit divergence, so it is out of this ticket's scope. Filing
it separately with `discovered_from`.
